newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia to host conference on Nile.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia to host conference on Nile.

text.p: Ethiopia will host a conference this month to boost cooperation between the 10 countries relying on the waters of the Nile river, officials said on Friday.
They said eight of the 10 states which rely on the Nile had so far said they would attend the Addis Ababa conference from February 24 to 28. Rwanda and Eritrea have not yet responded.
The other eight states which rely on the Nile are Burundi, Zaire, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Sudan, Egypt and Ethiopia.
The conference will discuss the right of all 10 states for fair and equitable distribution of the Nile, a basis for cooperation and a 1959 agreement between Sudan and Egypt on using its waters.
Ethiopia objects to the 1959 agreement dividing rights to use the Niles water between Egypt and Sudan.
The officials said Ethiopia would state its opposition to a World Bank directive that it should receive the support of other states using the Nile before going ahead with its development projects.
The Blue Nile originates in Ethiopias Lake Tana and travels about 1,500 km (900 miles) to Khartoum, where it joins the White Nile, which flows from Lake Victoria, Africas largest lake.
